points.description: States that the frequency of light is proportional to its energy (E = hν), so a given frequency means a given photon energy.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if the link is only implied or vaguely stated (e.g. 'frequency relates to energy' with no proportionality).

points.description: Electron energy levels in an atom are quantized (only certain discrete values), AND for excitation the photon energy (so frequency) must exactly equal the difference between two energy levels, so only certain frequencies are absorbed.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark for quantized levels stated without the exact-match link; 2 marks if the match to the energy difference is stated but 'quantized' or discrete levels is not.

points.description: Ejection needs a minimum energy (ionization energy / threshold frequency) to free the electron from the atom. Above this, the electron is no longer in a quantized bound level, so no exact match is needed.
points.partial_credit: 0.5 if the minimum energy is stated but not linked to ejection from the atom.

points.description: Any energy above the threshold is not absorbed into a level but becomes kinetic energy of the ejected electron, so any frequency above the threshold works.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if extra energy is said to go somewhere (e.g. 'excess energy is left over') without naming kinetic energy of the electron.

rubric.notes: Full marks need each claim stated with its cause-and-effect link: the exact match of photon energy to the level gap for excitation, and extra energy becoming kinetic energy for ejection. Give part marks only where the partial_credit line allows, for ideas stated halfway or vaguely. Restating the question or defining terms earns nothing; a wrong statement loses that point only.
